assign.request: Build /layouts/ - the encyclopedia, the global reference standard, the namespace for layouts. A layout's id is N-name: N is the number of columns at the widest, the name says how the room is divided. Every word defined so it describes many layouts. Every tag clickable to everything that carries it. A wireframe drawing class; one page per layout drawn at 400 / 1920 / 3440.
assign.now: scoping - reading the lab, the framework words, the owner's sentences
steps: Read the lab, the framework layout words, decide the namespace rules
layouts.json - the entries and the words that define them
Layout.js - the wireframe drawing class + doc/wire.md
/layouts/ - one screen: two sentences, then the tree
/layouts/<id>/ - routed from the json, drawn at 400/1920/3440
Map imagine/layouts onto ids; one link line in its readme
Proof: screenshots at 400 and 1920, zero console errors

log.msg: zoom scaling verified headless: a frame with container-type inline-size + aspect-ratio, drawing at width:Wpx with zoom: calc(100cqw / (W*1px)) - a 16em rail measured 40.0px in a 300px frame at 1920 and 76.8px at 400, exact. No container query on the drawing itself.

THE MAPPING - /imagine/layouts/ system.js: 18 arrangements map onto 8 ids. 1.stack=1-flow | 1.measure=1-centered | 1.rows=1-rows | 1.sections=1-bands+scroll snap | 2.equal=2-equal | 2.golden=2-sidebar+golden | 2.main-aside=2-sidebar+fluid | 2.fixed-fluid=2-sidebar+fixed width | 2.fr=2-sidebar+2 column grid | 3.thirds=3-equal | 3.rail-main-aside=3-holy-grail | 3.card=3-holy-grail | 3.rows-in-columns=3-holy-grail+nested rows | 3.scroll=3-holy-grail+split | 4.quarters=4-equal | 4.quad=2-equal with each column split into rows | 4.wall=n-wall | 4.shell=1-rows holding 3-holy-grail. The other ten were the same division wearing a proportion, a technique or a composition.

DECISION - the seed word N-cards resolves to the TAG cards (paint: a visible background and padding per column, gap usual not required) rather than an id, because an id names the DIVISION of the room and cards is paint. Defined that way the word describes 5 layouts instead of 1, which is the owner's own test answered. 3-cards / 2-cards / 4-cards / n-cards all kept as aliases and all are working urls landing on the right entry.

DECISION - a fourth branch `n` added to the tree: the layouts whose column count is not a number because the layout names a column WIDTH and the room decides (n-wall, n-newspaper). The owner's rule is `the first number is number of columns`; picking a fake number for a wall would have been a lie.

DECISION - one entry keeps a number: 4-1, the bento/mosaic grid. bento is a fashion word not a description of how the room divides, so it is an alias; mosaic is recorded as a CANDIDATE word, not adopted. This is the namespace's escape hatch working.

FENCE - css prefix `std-` censused clean (zero hits in public/ for .std*), deliberately not one letter from layouts- (/imagine/layouts) or layout- (ext/layout). NOT written into framework/styles/css-scopes.txt: that file is outside this task's write fence and shared with agents in flight. The line to add: `std-   /layouts (the layout standard)`. Recorded in layouts.css, readme.md and doc/decisions.md.

assign.outcome:
**/layouts/ is live — 13 layouts named, defined and drawn; 47 tags, every one clickable.**

An id is `N-name`: the number is how many columns at the widest, the name says how the room is divided. Names are CSS-agnostic, so a flex row and a grid that make the same picture are one layout and the technique is a tag.

![the tree](./shots/tree-1920.jpg)

**The tree** — `1:` flow · centered · rows · bands  ·  `2:` equal · sidebar  ·  `3:` equal · holy-grail · sidebar  ·  `4:` equal · 4-1  ·  `n:` wall · newspaper. [/layouts/](/layouts/)

**The owner's own question, answered.** *"'3-cards' what does this mean? can we define the word in a way that it's most useful to describe many layouts?"* — `cards` is **paint** (a visible background and padding on each column; a gap usual, not required), so it is a **tag**, not an id, and it describes five layouts instead of one: [/layouts/tag/cards/](/layouts/tag/cards/). `3-cards` still works as a url — every alias does.

**The rule everything hangs on:** an id names the DIVISION of the room. Paint, proportion, technique and side are tags. [doc/naming](/layouts/doc/naming/)

**One layout keeps a number.** [`4-1`](/layouts/4-1/) — the bento/mosaic grid. `bento` is a fashion word, not a description of how the room divides, so it is an alias and `mosaic` is recorded as a candidate. That entry is the namespace's escape hatch, working.

**Every layout is drawn at 400 / 1920 / 3440, side by side, on one height** — real flex and real grid at a real viewport width, shrunk with `zoom` inside a frame that carries the container-query unit. A 16em rail measures exactly 40.0px in a 300px frame at 1920. [2-sidebar](/layouts/2-sidebar/)

**The lab is mapped.** `/imagine/layouts/`'s eighteen arrangements are **eight** of these layouts; the other ten were the same division wearing a proportion, a technique or a composition. Table in [doc/decisions](/layouts/doc/decisions/); its readme now links the standard in its first line.

**Proof:** 16 urls x 2 widths headless — zero console errors, zero horizontal overflow, every h1 right. Six shots in `shots/`.

**Left, with reasons:** `std-` is not in `framework/styles/css-scopes.txt` (outside the write fence; the line to add is in the readme and in doc/decisions). Real websites are wired in but invisible until the corpus fills — every tag and layout page already reads `/websites/site/index.json` and draws nothing when it is absent.
